chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'O my Master! I hope to fast in Medina during the month of Ramadan.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'You will fast in it, if Allah wills.' I said, 'And I hope that our departure will be in the first ten days of Shawwal, and Allah has accustomed me to visiting the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and his Household, and visiting you. So perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of your father, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of my father, and perhaps I will perform Hajj on behalf of a man from my brothers, and perhaps I will perform Hajj for myself. So what should I do?' He said, 'Perform Tamattu'.' I said, 'I have been residing in Mecca for ten years.' So he said, 'Perform Tamattu'.'

key_terms.تَمَتَّعْ: Perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between)
key_terms.عَشْرٍ مِنْ شَوَّالٍ: The first ten days of Shawwal

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Tamattu' Hajj for a long-term resident of Mecca or when performing multiple Hajjs?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the ruling of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* for those residing in Mecca, such as the narrator who had lived there for ten years, confirming that the combination of Umrah and Hajj remains valid regardless of prolonged residence. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the performance of Hajj on behalf of others (for oneself, parents, or peers) while maintaining the specific ritual structure of Tamattu'. This underscores the Imam's authority in defining ritual forms even for long-term residents who might otherwise be considered *Muqim* (residents) rather than *Muhrim* (pilgrims in Ihram).
